defmodule AshPhoenix.Form do
  @moduledoc """
  A module to allow you to fluidly use resources with Phoenix forms.

  ### Life cycle

  The general workflow is, with either LiveView or Phoenix forms:

  1. Create a form with `AshPhoenix.Form`
  2. Render the form with `Phoenix.Component.form` (or `CoreComponents.simple_form`), or, if using Surface, `<Form>`
  3. To validate the form (e.g with `phx-change` for liveview), pass the submitted params to `AshPhoenix.Form.validate/3`
  4. On form submission, pass the params to `AshPhoenix.Form.submit/2`
  5. On success, use the result to redirect or assign. On failure, reassign the provided form.

  The following keys exist on the form to show where in the lifecycle you are:

  - `submitted_once?` - If the form has ever been submitted. Useful for not showing any errors on the first attempt to fill out a form.
  - `just_submitted?` - If the form has just been submitted and *no validation* has happened since. Useful for things like
    triggering a UI effect that should stop when the form is modified again.
  - `.changed?` - If something about the form is different than it originally was. Note that in some cases this can yield a
    false positive, specifically if a nested form is removed and then a new one is added with the exact same values.
  - `.touched_forms` - A MapSet containing all keys in the form that have been modified. When submitting a form, only these keys are included in the parameters.

  ### Forms in the code interface

  Throughout this documentation you will see forms created with `AshPhoenix.Form.for_create/3` and other functions like it.
  This is perfectly fine to do, however there is a way to use `AshPhoenix.Form` in a way that adds clarity to its usage
  and makes it easier to find usage of each action. Code interfaces allow us to do this for standard action calls, i.e:

  ```elixir
  resources do
    resource MyApp.Accounts.User do
      define :register_with_password, args: [:email, :password]
      define :update_user, action: :update, args: [:email, :password]
    end
  end
  ```

  Adding the `AshPhoenix` extension to our domains and resources, like so:

  ```elixir
  use Ash.Domain,
    extensions: [AshPhoenix]
  ```

  will cause another function to be generated for each definition, beginning with `form_to_`.

  By default, the `args` option in `define` is ignored when building forms. If you want to have
  positional arguments, configure that in the `forms` section which is added by the `AshPhoenix`
  section. For example:

  ```elixir
  forms do
    form :update_user, args: [:email]
  end
  ```

  With this extension, the standard setup for forms looks something like this:

  ```elixir
  def render(assigns) do
    ~H\"""
    <.form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">
      <.input field={@form[:email]} />
      <.input field={@form[:password]} />
      <.button type="submit" />
    </.form>
    \"""
  end

  def mount(_params, _session, socket) do
    # Here we call our new generated function to create the form
    {:ok, assign(socket, form: MyApp.Accounts.form_to_register_with_password() |> to_form())}
  end

  def handle_event("validate", %{"form" => params}, socket) do
    form = AshPhoenix.Form.validate(socket.assigns.form, params)
    {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, form)}
  end

  def handle_event("submit", %{"form" => params}, socket) do
    case AshPhoenix.Form.submit(socket.assigns.form, params: params) do
      {:ok, _user} ->
        socket =
          socket
          |> put_flash(:success, "User registered successfully")
          |> push_navigate(to: ~p"/")

        {:noreply, socket}

      {:error, form} ->
        socket =
          socket
          |> put_flash(:error, "Something went wrong")
          |> assign(:form, form)

        {:noreply, socket}
    end
  end
  ```

  ## Working with related or embedded data

  See the [nested forms guide](/documentation/topics/nested-forms.md)

  ## Working with compound types
  Compound types, such as `Ash.Money`, will need some extra work to make it work.

  For instance, when working with the `Transfer` type in `AshDoubleEntry.Transfer`, it will have the `Ash.Money` type for `amount`. When rendering the forms, you should do as follows:
  ```
  <.input
      name={@form[:amount].name <> "[amount]"}
      id={@form[:amount].id <> "_amount"}
      label="Amount"
      value={if(@form[:amount].value, do: @form[:amount].value.amount)}
    />
    <.input
      type="select"
      name={@form[:amount].name <> "[currency]"}
      id={@form[:amount].id <> "_currency"}
      options={[:USD, :HKD, :EUR]}
      label="Currency"
      value={if(@form[:amount].value, do: @form[:amount].value.currency)}
    />
  ```

  ### Handling errors for composite inputs

  When working with composite inputs like the example above, you may need to map errors from the composite field
  to the individual input fields. The `post_process_errors` option can help with this:

  ```elixir
  AshPhoenix.Form.for_create(Transfer, :create,
    post_process_errors: fn _form, _path, {field, message, vars} ->
      # Map amount field errors to the amount input specifically
      case field do
        :amount ->
          # Could check the error message to determine which sub-field
          if String.contains?(message, "currency") do
            {:amount_currency, message, vars}
          else
            {:amount_amount, message, vars}
          end
        _ ->
          # you can return `nil`
          {field, message, vars}

  def stop(resource, tenant \\ nil) do
    tenant =
      if Ash.Resource.Info.multitenancy_strategy(resource) == :context do
        tenant
      end

    if Ash.DataLayer.Ets.Info.private?(resource) do
      case Process.get({:ash_ets_table, resource, tenant}) do
        nil ->
          :ok

        table ->
          ETS.Set.delete(table)
      end
    else
      table =
        if tenant && Ash.Resource.Info.multitenancy_strategy(resource) == :context do
          String.to_atom(to_string(tenant) <> to_string(resource))
        else
          resource
        end

      name = Module.concat(table, TableManager)

      case Process.whereis(name) do
        nil ->
          :ok

        pid ->
          Process.exit(pid, :shutdown)
      end
    end
  end

  def do_sort_forms(forms, [], indices, name, id) when is_list(forms) and is_list(indices) do
    indices =

  end

  def do_sort_forms([], _, _, _, _), do: []

  def do_sort_forms(forms, [index], :increment, name, id) when is_list(forms) do
    index =
      if is_binary(index) do
        String.to_integer(index)
      else
        index
      end

    case Enum.split(forms, index) do
      {_head, [_]} ->
        forms

      {head, [first, second | rest]} ->
        reindex_sorted_forms(head ++ [second | [first | rest]], name, id)
    end
  end

  def do_sort_forms(forms, [index], :decrement, name, id) when is_list(forms) do
    index =
      if is_binary(index) do
        String.to_integer(index)
      else
        index
      end

    case Enum.split(forms, index) do
      {[], _} ->
        forms

      {head, [first | rest]} ->
        {head, [last]} = Enum.split(head, -1)
        reindex_sorted_forms(head ++ [first, last] ++ rest, name, id)
    end
  end

defmodule P do
  @re ~r/\[(?<key>[^\]]+)\](?:\[(?<index>[0-9]+)\])?/
  def parse(path) do
    Regex.scan(@re, path, capture: [:key, :index])
    |> Enum.map(fn [k, idx] -> {String.to_existing_atom(k), if(idx != "", do: String.to_integer(idx))} end)
  end
  def sort_path(steps) do
    Enum.reduce(steps, [], fn {k, idx}, acc ->
      acc = acc ++ [to_string(k)]
      if idx, do: acc ++ [Integer.to_string(idx)], else: acc
    end)
  end
end

defmodule Catering.Forms do
  @moduledoc """
  Facade that the LiveView layer uses to build, mutate, inspect and submit the
  nested catering order form.

  Everything reachable through plain function calls (no HTTP server/browser needed).

  ## Usage

      form = Catering.Forms.new_order_form()
      form = Catering.Forms.change(form, %{"reference" => "ord-1", "note" => "Delivery by noon"})

      form = Catering.Forms.add_nested(form, "order[line_items]", seed: %{"dish" => "a", "position" => 0})
      {:ok, order} = Catering.Forms.save(form)

  ## Path format

  Every `path` argument is one of the full HTML names of a nested form, rooted
  at `"order"` — e.g. `"order"`, `"order[line_items]"`,
  `"order[line_items][0]"`, `"order[line_items][0][modifiers]"`,
  `"order[line_items][0][modifiers][1]"`, `"order[customer]"`,
  `"order[delivery_windows][0]"`, `"order[fulfillment]"`.
  """

  alias AshPhoenix.Form
  alias Catering.Orders.Order

  # The name and id of the root form, as required by the task. This makes nested
  # form names match the exact HTML paths (order[line_items][0], etc.).
  @root_name "order"

  # Matches a key+index segment of a path, e.g. [line_items] or [line_items][0].
  # Named capture so we can extract key and index by name, and positional order
  # is stable (key before index) for path flattening.
  @path_re ~r/\[(?<key>[^\]]+)\](?:\[(?<index>[0-9]+)\])?/

  @doc "A blank create form for the order graph."
  def new_order_form do
    Form.for_create(Order, :place, name: @root_name)
    |> rename()
  end

  @doc "An update form for the stored order, with nested children sorted by position."
  def edit_order_form(order_id) do
    order = read_order!(order_id)
    Form.for_update(order, :revise, name: @root_name)
    |> rename()
  end

  @doc "The `%Phoenix.HTML.Form{}` for a form."
  def to_phoenix_form(form), do: Form.to_phoenix_form(form)

  @doc "Revalidate a form against a fresh parameter map. Optional options forwarded to ash_phoenix."
  def change(form, params, opts \\ []), do: Form.validate(form, params, opts)

  @doc "Add a nested form at a path. Optional options seed params, insert at front, or override action type."
  def add_nested(form, path, opts \\ []) do
    # add_form inserts a new form at the path's parent, optionally validating.
    # opts are forwarded to the underlying ash_phoenix op (seed, at_front, create_action/read_action, validate?).
    Form.add_form(form, path, opts)
  end

  @doc "Remove the nested form at a path."
  def remove_nested(form, path) do
    Form.remove_form(form, path)
  end

  @doc "Reorder the nested list at a path given a list of its current zero-based indices."
  def reorder(form, path, order) do
    do_sort_forms(form, path, order)
  end

  @doc "Move the nested form at a path one slot earlier (`:up`) or later (`:down`)."
  def move(form, path, direction) do
    instruction = case direction do
      :up -> :decrement
      :down -> :increment
      other -> raise ArgumentError, "direction must be :up or :down, got: #{inspect other}"
    end

    do_sort_forms(form, path, instruction)
  end

  @doc "The parameter map that would be sent to the underlying action."
  def submitted_params(form) do
    Form.submitted_params(form)
  end

  @doc "The hidden inputs required to render the form at a path."
  def hidden_inputs(form, path) do
    form
    |> find_form!(path)
    |> Form.hidden_fields()
    |> Map.new(fn {field, value} -> {to_string(field), to_string(value)} end)
  end

  @doc "User-facing errors keyed by the HTML name of the form that owns them, `[field, message]` sorted ascending."
  def error_map(form) do
    form
    |> gather_form_errors()
    |> Map.new(fn {name, errors} ->
      sorted = Enum.sort(errors)
      {name, sorted}
    end)
  end

  @doc "Untranslated errors of the form at a path as `{field, message, vars}` tuples, sorted by field then message."
  def raw_error_list(form, path) do
    form
    |> find_form!(path)
    |> Form.raw_errors(for_path: [])
    |> Enum.sort_by(fn {field, message, _vars} -> {field, message} end)
  end

  @doc "A deterministic, plain-data snapshot of the whole form tree."
  def serialize(form) do
    %{
      "name" => form.name,
      "id" => form.id,
      "type" => to_string(form.type),
      "resource" => inspect(form.resource),
      "valid" => form.valid? == true,
      "hidden" => Map.new(hidden_inputs(form, form.name), fn {k, v} -> {k, to_string(v)} end),
      "values" => serialize_values(form),
      "errors" => Enum.sort(get_own_errors(form)),
      "nested" => serialize_nested(form)
    }
  end

  @doc "Submit the form and persist the graph (or validate + submit with params). Returns `{:ok, order}` or `{:error, form}`."
  def save(form, params \\ nil) do
    case params do
      nil -> Form.submit(form)
      params -> form |> Form.validate(params) |> Form.submit()
    end
  end

  # --- Internal helpers ---

  defp rename(form), do: %{form | name: @root_name, id: @root_name}

  defp read_order!(id) do
    Ash.read_one!(Order |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^id),
      load: [line_items: :modifiers]
    )
  end

  # Sorts the nested list at `path` via the underlying ash_phoenix sort engine.
  # Path is a HTML name string, `instruction` is a list of indices (reorder) or
  # :increment/:decrement (move).
  defp do_sort_forms(form, path, instruction) do
    sort_keys = path |> parse_path() |> sort_path()
    Form.sort_forms(form, sort_keys, instruction)
  end

  # HTML name string -> list of {key :: String, index :: integer | nil} steps.
  defp parse_path(path) do
    Regex.scan(@path_re, path, capture: [:key, :index])
    |> Enum.map(fn [k, idx] ->
      idx = if idx != "", do: String.to_integer(idx)
      {k, idx}
    end)
  end

  # Path steps -> flat list of string keys/indices, suitable for do_sort_forms.
  defp sort_path(steps) do
    Enum.reduce(steps, [], fn {k, idx}, acc ->
      acc = acc ++ [k]
      if idx, do: acc ++ [Integer.to_string(idx)], else: acc
    end)
  end

  # Find the nested form exactly matching a path by name (rooted at order).
  # Forms nest in `.forms` as either a single form or a list of forms.
  defp find_form!(form, path) do
    case find_form(form, path) do
      {:ok, found} -> found
      nil -> raise "no form found at path #{inspect path}"
    end
  end

  defp find_form(form, path) do
    cond do
      form.name == path ->
        {:ok, form}

      forms = Map.get(form, :forms) ->
        Enum.find_value(forms, fn {_key, children} ->
          children
          |> List.wrap()
          |> Enum.find_value(fn child ->
            case find_form(child, path) do
              {:ok, found} -> {:ok, found}
              nil -> nil
            end
          end)
        end)

      true ->
        nil
    end
  end

  # Map of HTML name -> own errors (ignoring nested) for every form in the tree.
  defp gather_form_errors(form) do
    {%{}, []}
    |> gather_form_errors(form)
    |> elem(0)
  end

  defp gather_form_errors({map, trail}, form) do
    map = case get_own_errors(form) do
      [] -> map
      errors -> Map.put(map, form.name, errors)
    end

    Enum.reduce(Map.get(form, :forms) || %{}, {map, trail}, fn {_key, children}, acc ->
      Enum.reduce(List.wrap(children), acc, &gather_form_errors(&2, &1))
    end)
  end

  defp get_own_errors(form) do
    case Form.errors(form, for_path: [], format: :raw) do
      errors when is_list(errors) ->
        for {field, {message, _}} <- errors, do: [to_string(field), message]

      _ ->
        []
    end
  end

  defp serialize_values(form) do
    values = form.params || %{}

    form.form_keys
    |> Enum.reject(fn {_key, config} -> config[:embed?] || config[:for_type] end)
    |> Map.new(fn {key, config} ->
      val = Map.get(values, to_string(config[:for] || key))
      {to_string(config[:for] || key), if(val != nil, do: to_string(val), else: nil)}
    end)
  end

  defp serialize_nested(form) do
    Map.new(Map.get(form, :forms) || %{}, fn {key, children} ->
      {to_string(key), case children do
        l when is_list(l) -> Enum.map(l, &serialize/1)
        single -> serialize(single)
      end}
    end)
  end
end
